note: Escalated by the 07:14 yield round: the group whitelist says EXPECTED-DISABLED for eight Bigmoney tasks but never says which machine owns each lane, so a name-keyed enable at the 2026-11-08 review could start one lane on two machines. Verified by scripts/lane_host_ownership.py -- it re-reads the whitelist from the group origin blob, each register script under Tools/, and each target script's own owner constant, and refuses a row it cannot see.

tasks.note: the watchdog C8 supply driver; each machine fills its own share of the pool, so one instance per machine is the design, two instances on one machine is the defect
the only one of the eight that is a single-host lane in code: LANE_OWNER = bm-b and the script's own lane guard turns every other machine into a stdout-only no-op
the register script carries the pinned start offsets bm-a=8 / bm-b=2 / bm-c=5, which only makes sense if all three machines run it
a per-machine watchdog can only revive the loop on the machine it runs on, so it must exist everywhere the loop does
register script spreads worker start offsets over all three hosts (bm-a=7 / bm-b=12 / bm-c=17)
writes a machine-suffixed state face (results/dispatcher_state.<mid>.json), so instances are meant to coexist

per-machine engine (each machine burns its own queue), but the task name is the fleet-shared local name and pins bm-b: found Disabled on bm-a, a name-keyed restore would enable bm-b's engine on the wrong machine and leave bm-a's own engine without a task -- so the enable action must resolve the host from fleet/machine.json, never from the task name

the eighth owner=@BigMoney row is this one, not HQ-Patrol-BigMoney (that row's owner is @HQ): it runs bm-a's own work bank and bm-a's SatEngine revive recipe, and there is a separate bmb_idleguard.pyw for bm-b, so the two machines have two tasks and no shared lane
